zh.title: 長榮航空9月29日起調漲國際線超額行李費
zh.summary: 長榮航空9月29日起調整國際線行李費率，超額行李每件最高調漲至390美元。
body: 長榮航空宣布，自2026年9月29日起調整國際線行李政策與費率。調整項目涵蓋超額行李、預付超額行李、超重及超尺寸行李的費率與計價規範，寵物與運動器材的收費標準也將同步進行調整。
長榮航空指出，本次費率調整主要是受到國際經濟環境及地緣政治因素影響，旨在反映航空燃油價格以及整體全球營運成本的上升。
在超額行李部分，費率劃分為台灣及5個區域，收費從原本每件140美元至300美元，調漲為160美元至390美元，各區域調幅約在20美元至90美元不等。

en.title: EVA Air to Raise International Excess Baggage Fees Starting Sept. 29
en.summary: EVA Air will adjust international baggage rates on Sept. 29, raising excess baggage fees to $160-$390.
body: EVA Air has announced that it will adjust its international baggage policy and fee structure starting September 29, 2026. The changes apply to excess baggage, prepaid excess baggage, overweight and oversized baggage rates, as well as fee standards for pets and sports equipment.

According to the airline, the rate adjustments respond to international economic conditions and geopolitical factors, reflecting rising aviation fuel prices and higher overall global operational costs.

Under the updated policy, excess baggage rates are divided into Taiwan and five geographical zones. Per-piece charges will increase from $140-$300 USD to $160-$390 USD, representing an increase of $20 to $90 USD depending on the region.

zh.title: 日本畫作於檀香山停機坪雨淋受損 阿拉斯加航空挨告索賠
zh.summary: 阿拉斯加航空因11幅日本畫作於檀香山受雨勢損壞，遭索賠521900美元。
body: 阿拉斯加航空（Alaska Airlines）目前正面臨一項金額達521,900美元的法律訴訟。根據航空新聞媒體 Simple Flying 報導，該起訴訟源於一批共11幅日本畫作，在夏威夷檀香山（Honolulu）運送期間遭遇雨勢，最終造成畫作嚴重受損。
報導指出，這批受損貨物包含脆弱的紙質畫作，在檀香山出現傾盆大雨期間，被留置暴露於戶外停機坪上。相關原告隨後針對貨物毀損狀況提出法律訴訟，向阿拉斯加航空要求索賠521,900美元賠償金。

en.title: Alaska Airlines Sued for $521,900 Over Damaged Japanese Paintings in Honolulu
en.summary: Alaska Airlines faces a $521,900 lawsuit after 11 Japanese paintings were damaged by rain in Honolulu.
body: Alaska Airlines is facing a legal claim seeking $521,900 in compensation after 11 Japanese paintings were ruined during a severe rainstorm in Honolulu. According to a report by Simple Flying, the lawsuit was filed over extensive water damage suffered by the cargo shipment while in transit.

The shipment, consisting of fragile paper paintings, was reportedly left exposed on an airport ramp in Honolulu during heavy torrential rainfall. The legal action alleges that failing to protect the delicate artwork from rain caused severe damage, leading to the $521,900 compensation demand against Alaska Airlines.

zh.title: 肯亞航空代理CEO辭職 財務虧損擴大至160億
zh.summary: 代理CEO辭職；上半年虧損160億；燃油價漲66%；營收增9%
body: 肯亞航空代理執行長喬治·卡馬爾宣布辭職，將於9月30日前留任。
航空公司上半年淨虧損160.8億肯亞先令，營收同比增長9%達812.5億。
燃油價格飆漲66%成主要成本驅動因素，供應鏈限制亦影響機隊可用性。
新任代理執行長哈比爾·瓦斯瓦尼將於9月15日接任，擁有24年企業法律經驗。
卡馬爾曾任埃及航空、阿聯酋航空及阿拉伯航空高管，並曾擔任國際航空運輸協會顧問。
公司表示卡馬爾在任期間穩定營運，並成功度過最高層領導層更迭。

en.title: Kenya Airways Acting CEO Resigns Amid KSH16bn Half-Year Loss
en.summary: Acting CEO resigns; H1 net loss KSH16bn; fuel prices up 66%; revenue up 9%
body: Kenya Airways Acting CEO George Kamal has announced his resignation and will remain until 30 September 2026. The airline also faces strikes at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport (NBO).
Habil Waswani will become Acting Group Managing Director and CEO from 15 September, succeeding Kamal after a 15-day transition.
The carrier reported a net loss of KSH 16.08 billion for the first half of 2026, despite a 9% revenue increase to KSH 81.25 billion.
Jet fuel prices surged 66% in the period, driven by Middle East tensions, while supply‑chain constraints reduced aircraft availability.

zh.title: 波音MH-139A灰狼達初始作戰能力 接替UH-1N執行核彈安全任務
zh.summary: MH-139A灰狼8月10日達IOC；首度護航民兵三型車隊；速度快50%、載員倍增
body: 美國空軍全球打擊司令部（AFGSC）的波音MH-139A灰狼直升機於2026年8月10日達成初始作戰能力（IOC），正式開始取代服役超過五十年的UH-1N休伊直升機，執行洲際彈道飛彈（ICBM）發射場的核安全任務。這項里程碑標誌著美國陸基核威嚇力量的空中支援能力邁入新階段。
MH-139A以商用的李奧納多AW139直升機為基礎，由波音依軍規改裝而成。根據空軍聲明，灰狼的巡航速度比UH-1N快近50%，可攜帶雙倍兵力，並具備增強防禦系統與前視紅外線感測器，大幅提升對廣大飛彈基地的快速反應與態勢感知能力。
以蒙大拿州馬姆斯特洛姆空軍基地為例，其飛彈綜合體佔地約13,800平方英里（35,740平方公里），擁有逾百個發射設施。龐大的防禦區域使得直升機的速度、航程與載員量成為關鍵，灰狼的性能優勢正是為因應這類地理挑戰而設計。
2026年1月，第40直升機中隊的兩架MH-139A首度執行實戰護航任務，陪同民兵三型飛彈維修與裝甲安保車隊往返距離基地超過100英里（160公里）的發射設施，全程約六小時且無需空中加油。這次任務實證了灰狼在長距離護航中的持久作戰能力。
除護航外，灰狼還負責核安全突發事件的快速反應、發射設施奪回與恢復等任務。空軍測試已涵蓋護航支援、緊急反應及設施奪回等情境，旨在驗證機組人員能多快起飛並將戰術部隊投送至需加強安保的地點。

en.title: Boeing MH-139A Grey Wolf reaches IOC, replaces UH-1N for US nuclear missile security
en.summary: Grey Wolf achieves IOC; first Minuteman III convoy escort; 50% faster, double troop capacity
body: The Boeing MH-139A Grey Wolf helicopter achieved Initial Operational Capability (IOC) on 10 August 2026, marking the start of its operational replacement of the Vietnam-era UH-1N Huey in the US Air Force Global Strike Command’s nuclear security mission. The milestone signals a new era for airborne support of America’s land-based nuclear deterrent.

The MH-139A is derived from the commercial Leonardo AW139, modified by Boeing for military requirements. According to a USAF statement, the Grey Wolf is nearly 50% faster than the UH-1N, can carry twice as many troops, and incorporates enhanced defensive systems and a forward-looking infrared sensor, significantly improving speed, payload, and situational awareness across vast missile fields.

The operational need is driven by geography. At Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana, for example, the missile complex covers approximately 13,800 square miles (35,740 square kilometres) and includes more than 100 launch facilities. The Grey Wolf’s combination of speed, range, and capacity is designed to meet the demands of patrolling and responding across such expansive terrain.

The type flew its first operational convoy in January 2026, when two aircraft from the 40th Helicopter Squadron escorted a Minuteman III maintenance and armoured security convoy to a launch facility more than 100 miles (160 kilometres) east of Malmstrom and back, completing the six-hour mission without refuelling. The sortie demonstrated the Grey Wolf’s endurance for long-distance convoy support.

Beyond convoy escort, the Grey Wolf is tasked with rapid emergency response and the recapture and recovery of launch facilities. USAF testing has examined scenarios covering convoy support, emergency response, and facility recapture, validating the helicopter’s ability to deploy tactical security forces quickly across difficult terrain.
